 "content": "# Continual-ARC: opposite-edge row encoding (observed task)

## Reusable rule from task-93da8cad

When a grid has two opposing edge segments of the same marker color, and a different-colored seed lies on a row within one segment:

1. The seed's row, measured by its offset within its edge segment, selects the corresponding row in the opposite edge segment (same offset from that segment's start). Paint that entire opposite-segment row across the interior with the seed color, preserving the edge marker.
2. On the seed's own row, fill between the seed and its adjacent edge marker with the seed color; change the seed cell to color 4. Leave other cells unchanged.

The two example segments were opposite vertical edges, so the resulting fills were horizontal. Segment-relative offsets matter; the segments need not begin at the same absolute row.

## Evidence

Demo: 30x8, background 7, edge-marker color 2. Right edge segment rows 0–13; opposite left segment rows 14–27. Seeds (color 1) in the left segment at rows 14,17,18,19,20,21,23,24,25,26. Corresponding right-segment rows 0,3,4,5,6,7,9,10,11,12 were filled across interior with 1. Each seed row was filled from the left edge to the seed and seed changed to 4.

Solved test: 20x23, background 6, edge-marker color 9. Left segment rows 0–5; opposite right segment rows 10–15. Seed color 8 at (row 14, col 6), offset 4 within its segment. Thus right-segment corresponding row 14? More precisely opposite left segment offset 4 is row 4: row 4 was filled across interior with 8. On seed row 14, cells from the seed toward right edge were filled with 8, and seed became 4. Submission was confirmed correct.

Generalization is based on one demonstrated task and one confirmed test; verify segment orientation/offset carefully on future variants."
